extracted.intended_audience: State and Federal Health Insurance Exchanges, QHP issuers, agents/brokers/web-brokers, consumer assisters, and stakeholders submitting comments on Exchange rules
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of proposed regulatory standards and operational requirements for Health Insurance Exchanges (automatic re-enrollment, premium payment thresholds, and open enrollment period) as presented in a proposed HHS rule. Focuses on what Exchanges, issuers, and intermediaries must or must not do and the policy rationales for those requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active confirmation for fully-subsidized APTC enrollees during redetermination
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to require qualified enrollees who are redetermined to be eligible for APTC that fully subsidizes their premium to take an active step to confirm their eligibility information before continuing with fully subsidized coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: growth in survey undercounts and research on misreporting (people unknowingly retaining coverage, multiple coverages) indicates many people remain enrolled without awareness. The proposed requirement aims to address program integrity by preventing continuance of fully subsidized coverage without the enrollee's affirmative confirmation. The agency seeks comment on this proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove bronze-to-silver automatic crosswalk (§155.335(j)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to remove §155.335(j)(4) which currently allows Exchanges to move a CSR-eligible enrollee from a bronze QHP into a silver QHP (same product/provider network and lower or equivalent net premium) without the enrollee's active participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context and rationale: the bronze-to-silver crosswalk was intended to give CSR-eligible enrollees access to more generous cost-sharing at the same or lower net premium. However, increased consumer awareness of subsidies, impending expiration of enhanced subsidies, commenters' concerns about consumer choice, potential tax liability, and undermining trust have led to the conclusion that terminating an enrollee's chosen bronze coverage without active participation is now more harmful than beneficial. Removal is proposed to better support consumer choice and honor prior selections. The agency requests comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve network-similarity consideration when plan unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the requirement that Exchanges take into account network similarity to an enrollee's current-year plan when re-enrolling an enrollee whose current plan is no longer available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although proposing to remove the crosswalk at §155.335(j)(4), the proposal leaves in place requirements that limit differences between the consumer's current plan and any alternative enrollment when the current plan is unavailable (e.g., consider provider network similarity). This is intended to limit disruption when re-enrollment into a different plan is necessary and to harmonize with guaranteed renewability provisions and state law where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit premium payment thresholds to net percentage-based only (§155.400(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to remove the fixed-dollar and gross percentage-based premium payment threshold options from §155.400(g), leaving issuers able to implement only the net percentage-based premium payment threshold (as established in prior notices and modified to allow issuers to set it at 95% of the net premium or higher).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: data showing continued high numbers of improper enrollments and the risk that fixed-dollar or gross percentage thresholds enable enrollees to remain enrolled for many months without paying (thereby obscuring improper enrollments) motivate the change. Examples given: a $1 enrollee premium could enable up to 9 months without payment under a $10 fixed threshold then another 3 months of grace; a 98% gross threshold can similarly delay delinquency. The net percentage threshold ensures enrollees always pay some premium to avoid delinquency, reducing the chance of prolonged improper enrollment and related harms. The agency notes burdens on issuers are outweighed by program integrity benefits and seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallow application of premium thresholds to binder payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification/criterion from existing policy that premium payment thresholds may not be applied to the binder payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under prior rules, the fixed-dollar and gross percentage-based thresholds could not be applied to binder payments; the proposal reiterates that binder payments are excluded from these threshold applications (and the removal of those threshold types would make this less relevant). This prevents issuers from treating binder payment as satisfying threshold rules that would avoid grace-period triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuer grace period and delinquency notice timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that QHP issuers provide a 3 consecutive month grace period for enrollees receiving APTC and provide notice of payment delinquency promptly, within 10 business days of when the issuer should have discovered the delinquency (§156.270(d) and (f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: ensure enrollees receive timely notice and are aware in advance of the risk of losing coverage if they do not take action to pay past due premiums. These safeguards remain part of the policy package balancing consumer protection with program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change Annual Open Enrollment Period to Nov 1 – Dec 15 for 2026+ (§155.410)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to amend §155.410(e) to set the Exchange annual individual market Open Enrollment Period (OEP) for benefit years starting January 1, 2026 and beyond to begin November 1 and end December 15 of the preceding calendar year, with an effective date of January 1 for QHP selections received on or before December 15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale and evidence: historically OEP dates were adjusted to balance adverse selection risk and consumer access. The December 15 end date reduces consumer confusion, aligns with employer-based plan deadlines, reduces casework and inadvertent dual enrollments, and promotes a full year of coverage. Experience with extended OEP (ending Jan 15) showed only a small fraction of enrollees changed coverage after Dec 15; data indicate limited consumer benefits from the extension relative to administrative burdens and possible improper enrollments. The agency also requests comment on whether to delay the effective date for this change because of special circumstances for PY 2026 (expiration of enhanced subsidies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh adverse selection, consumer confusion, and operational burden when setting OEP
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy criterion that setting OEP dates should balance the risk of adverse selection against ensuring consumers have adequate opportunity to enroll, while considering impacts on consumer confusion, issuer and Exchange operational burden, and assister capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical contexts: initial long OEP (Oct–Mar) provided time for outreach but increased adverse selection; later shorter windows aimed to limit adverse selection while enabling coverage. Considerations include enrollment patterns (majority enroll before Dec 15), alignment with other coverage deadlines, reduced casework when deadlines align, and the possibility that extending OEP increases late enrollments but may disproportionately help those receiving financial assistance. The agency used enrollment data across years and states to assess these tradeoffs and solicits comments on tradeoffs for PY 2026 and beyond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen program integrity to reduce improper enrollments (agents/brokers/web-brokers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy direction to adopt measures (e.g., removing flexible premium thresholds, requiring active confirmation for fully subsidized enrollees, revising re-enrollment rules) intended to reduce improper enrollments and the ability of third parties to enroll or keep enrollees in coverage without their knowledge or consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence and examples: large number of consumer complaints in 2023–2024 (e.g., 7,134 complaints in Dec 2024; high of 39,985 in Feb 2024), documented instances of Medicaid beneficiaries enrolled in QHPs without consent (44,151 complaints in 2024, 12,954 medically urgent). The proposal explains how certain threshold policies can incentivize agents/brokers to enroll consumers into plans that preserve commissions for longer, and that removal of those policies is expected to increase detection of improper enrollments and result in policy terminations in some cases (estimated ~184,111 terminations if fixed-dollar/gross thresholds removed). The agency seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use survey and enrollment data (undercounts, multiple coverage) to inform policy changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use empirical findings—e.g., CPS and NHIS undercounts of QHP enrollment increased substantially since 2021, and CBO estimates of people with multiple types of coverage—to justify policy proposals (e.g., active confirmation requirements) aimed at program integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data cited: CPS undercount for QHP with APTC grew from 25% (2021) to 50% (2024); undercount larger for incomes <250% FPL; NHIS undercount increased from ~14.1% (2022) to ~20.2% (Q1 2024). Evidence links increases in undercount to multiple coverage and to continuous enrollment processes (e.g., ARP expansion of fully subsidized QHPs and redetermination processes that do not require active participation). The agency uses these findings to infer likely increases in misreporting and to motivate proposals (active confirmation, premium threshold limits, re-enrollment rule changes).
